title: Starfish Regrow From One Arm
script: Starfish can clone themselves from just one arm. If a predator bites one off, it isn't just a lost limb. Most animals just heal a wound, but these creatures use specialized cells to rebuild from scratch. As long as a tiny piece of the central disc stays attached, that single arm grows a brand new mouth and four more limbs. It is the ultimate survival hack. Would you keep a spare arm around if it meant you could start over?

title: The Pufferfish Uses Its Fins To Draw Perfect Geometric Sand Circles
script: Ever wondered how a tiny pufferfish creates perfect geometric art? These little guys spend days dragging their bodies through the sand to build complex circular nests. They are literally the ocean's best architects. They don't have tools or rulers, just their tiny fins and a whole lot of patience. It is honestly mind-blowing to see such precise patterns underwater without a single mistake. Do you think you could draw a perfect circle in the sand without using any tools at all?

title: Coral Reefs Are Actually Massive Underwater Skeletons
script: Coral reefs are built from millions of tiny animal skeletons. You might think these reefs are just colorful rocks or plants, but they are living colonies. Each tiny creature, called a polyp, secretes a hard limestone shell around its body. Over thousands of years, these layers stack up to form the massive structures we see today. It is basically a giant, underwater skeleton city that protects the whole ocean ecosystem. Would you ever want to go scuba diving through a giant skeleton?
